newsitem.title: USA: Whitman unit head says wrongfully terminated.
newsitem.headline: Whitman unit head says wrongfully terminated.

text.p: William Frago, who until Wednesday was president and chief executive officer of Pepsi-Cola General Bottlers, told Reuters he was "wrongfully terminated" because of a clash over how the company's parent, Whitman Corp, handled political contributions.

"I believe I was wrongfully terminated because I refused to approve political contributions which were being channeled by Whitman Corp through Pepsi-Cola General Bottlers to avoid adverse media publicity," Frago said, reading from a statement.
"This was only the latest example of difficulties I have experienced with Whitman management regarding accurate disclosure of company operations," he added
Frago, who said he has retained an attorney, declined to elaborate but said of his firing, "I'm shocked and very surprised at this."

Whitman spokesman Charles Connelly said, "Political contributions have nothing to do with the reason Bill Frago was terminated. He simply could not provide the leadership we were looking for at Pepsi General."
Pepsi General, which Frago headed since April 15, 1996, accounts for more than half of all of Whitman's sales and earnings.

Frago, 54, was previously president of United Technologies Corp's Carrier Corp. Before that he was with General Electric Co's lighting business group in Cleveland as vice president-worldwide product management and marketing.
